headline: HiVe-Mem reports adaptive multimodal-memory retrieval with lower token use
summary: Zhang et al. introduce HiVe-Mem, which expands semantically retrieved interaction episodes through a text-and-visual affinity graph, then uses a PPO-trained selector to choose evidence forms per retrieved episode. In a preprint, they report higher F1 and LLM-judge scores than the compared multimodal memory systems on Mem-Gallery, WorldMemArena's Lifelong subset, and H2HMem, with 89.8–91.6% lower average token use than the most token-efficient multimodal baselines. These are author-reported benchmark results; the paper excludes adversarial settings, uses GPT-4o-mini for LLM judging, and has not been independently reproduced. The linked repository exposes implementation and experiment instructions, but the research desk did not run it.
